name: Non-Lucrative Visa (Visado de Residencia No Lucrativa)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires passive income (pensions, rentals, dividends, interest, annuities, or savings) of at least €2,400/month / €28,800/year (400% of the 2026 IPREM).
requirements.fix_path: Increase passive income to the required level.

value.note: additional income required per accompanying dependent

requirements.blocker_text: Each accompanying dependent adds a further €600/month (100% of IPREM) to the required income.
This does not permit any employed or self-employed work in Spain — income must be genuinely passive.
This requires private health insurance with coverage equivalent to the Spanish public system, with no copayments or waiting periods.
requirements.fix_path: Purchase a qualifying private health insurance policy.

evidence_required.document: Proof of passive income (pension statements, rental contracts, dividend/interest records)
Private health insurance policy meeting the no-copay/no-waiting-period standard
Clean criminal record certificate and medical certificate

outcome.duration_length: initial 1 year, renewable 2 years then 2 years

sources.title: Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores — Visado de Residencia No Lucrativa

notes: FORMULA VALUE, tier-1 confirmed as pegged to IPREM (not SMI) at exactly 400% for the main applicant, +100% per dependent. HIGH STALE-DATA RISK, same class as Portugal's RMMG-vs-IAS confusion: several tier-3 sites publish €31,200/year or ~€2,600/month, apparently computing 400% of the ANNUAL 14-payment IPREM figure (€8,400 × 4 = €33,600, still doesn't match either) rather than the correct monthly-times-12 convention actually used in consular practice (€600 × 4 × 12 = €28,800). This is the clearest single counterfeit-figure case in the Spain dataset. LIVE STRUCTURAL RISK worth flagging prominently: the IPREM has been FROZEN at €600/month since 2021 purely because Spain hasn't passed a new national budget (Presupuestos Generales del Estado) for 2024, 2025, or 2026 — any future budget passage would move this and several other Spain thresholds (family reunification, student) simultaneously in one event, unlike the UK/Germany/Netherlands/Portugal patterns where each threshold updates somewhat independently. citizenship_after_months (120) uses the general 10-year track since NLV holders aren't inherently tied to any nationality-based reduced track — Ibero-American/Andorran/Filipino/Equatorial-Guinean/Sephardic NLV holders would use the 2-year reduced track instead (see es_naturalisation).
